newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-MCNAMARA PUTS NEW SOUTH WALES IN CHARGE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MCNAMARA PUTS NEW SOUTH WALES IN CHARGE.

text.p: All-rounder Brad McNamara scored an unbeaten century as New South Wales took charge of their Shefffield Shield match against Tasmania on Saturday.
McNamara returned with the new ball later in the day to trap Tasmanian opener Dene Hills leg before wicket for 11.
Tasmania ended the second day on 148 for three in reply to the visitors' first innings 403 for nine declared at Bellerive Oval in Hobart.
McNamara hit 18 fours and one six in his unbeaten innings of 137, his highest score in first-class cricket.
He added 138 runs in a last-wicket partnership with paceman Phil Alley, who contributed 54 not out. It was the seventh highest 10-wicket stand in first-class cricket in Australia.
In Brisbane, Victoria were 54 without loss in their second innings against Queensland at close of play at the Gabba.
Victoria, who made 162 on Friday, dismissed Queensland for 305, with Andrew Symonds hitting 77 to earn his side a commanding first innings lead.
In Adelaide, former test batsman Justin Langer scored 116 as Western Australia were 318 all out in reply to South Australia's first innings 277.
At close of play at Adelaide Oval, the home side were 27 for one.
